title: Sirop de tamarin (Tamarind Syrup)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: A kilogram of tamarind soaked in 1½ litres of water 10 minutes, macerated, filtered and boiled 20 minutes with a kilogram of sugar; diluted at 1 volume of syrup to 5 volumes of water.
longDesc: p. 75 of the October 2023 recipe book: 1 kg tamarind fruit, 1 kg sugar and 1.5 litres of water. The fruit is soaked in the 1½ litres of drinking water 10 minutes, macerated, filtered, the sugar added and the syrup boiled 20 minutes, then cooled and kept cool. To drink: ‘take one volume of syrup for 5 volumes of water’. The book again calls it a ‘laxative par excellence’ (unsourced). The diagram says ‘Cuisson (65°)’ and shows no sugar, in conflict with the text; recorded, not reconciled. The syrup is described as unpasteurised.
steps: Soak the fruit in 1½ litres of drinking water for 10 minutes.
Add the sugar and boil 20 minutes.
To serve, dilute at 1 volume of syrup to 5 volumes of water.
chefTips: The printed dilution is 1 volume of syrup to 5 volumes of water.
The diagram’s 65° and missing sugar conflict with the text.
The syrup is unpasteurised, so keep it cold.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the sugar in the boil.
storage: Keep cool (‘conserver au frais’). No shelf life is printed.
healthBenefits: The book claims a laxative effect; it cites no evidence.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Sirop de tamarin’ (p. 75). Authors as printed: ‘Tata Ngome et al.’ (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré; ReSI-NoC project); October 2023 (V1), © 2024, CC BY 4.0. Yield not printed for any recipe in the book. Servings 15 is a placeholder. TWO-PASS.
CONFLICT (unreconciled): the diagram shows ‘Cuisson (65°)’ with no sugar step against 20 minutes of boiling with sugar in the text. ABSENT: shelf life.
